sentences.why: Source distinguishes crude price (Hormuz headline risk) from refined-product/crack-spread levels (the physical shortage), which have diverged to record levels — matches the sentence's framing that the two have come apart.

sentences.span: any resolution to the conflict or de-escalation of the conflict could bring much lower energy prices and inflation prints
sentences.why: MS frames Middle East de-escalation/resolution as the scenario that sharply lowers oil, consistent with the sentence's claim that a ceasefire read reprices barrels the market has feared losing; sentence dramatizes MS's conditional risk scenario but preserves its substance and conditional nature.

sentences.span: Jared Cohen (President of Global Affairs & Co-Head, GS Global Institute) on US-China: ... remove that shock absorber and GIR says fair value is roughly $10-15 higher
sentences.why: The 'fair value' oil estimate attributed to JPMorgan is Goldman Sachs' own GIR estimate (Jared Cohen, GS Global Institute), published in a Goldman Sachs note. No JPMorgan-sourced document exists anywhere in the day's file set — 'who said it' has been changed to a bank that never appears as a source.

sentences.span: Following last week's hike by the European Central Bank, both the Federal Reserve (Fed) and the Bank of Japan (BoJ) are expected to raise rates this week
sentences.why: Multiple central banks (ECB, Fed, BoJ) did hike in the relevant window per sources; the sentence's claim is explicitly conditional ('If that read is right'), matching the hedged, scenario-based framing used by the sources themselves.

sentences.why: Both the Trump-Xi framing and the fair-value premium figure come from Goldman Sachs (GS Global Institute, inside a GS Crook note), not JPMorgan — no JPMorgan document exists in the source set at all. Additionally, no source anywhere supports BofA holding a short position in 2-year Treasuries ($SHY) on a 'not restrictive enough' view; that clause has zero source support.

sentences.span: Markets are now pricing in a greater than 50% chance of a hike in October
sentences.why: MS's 'greater than 50% chance' is reasonably characterized colloquially as a 'coin flip'; no source states a materially different (e.g. strongly skewed) probability.

The precise figure 4.744% in the sources belongs to a Commerzbank/AXALEM corporate bond's yield-to-worst, not the 2-year US Treasury yield. The only actual 2-year UST reference found is MS's 'approaching 4.75%' — a real but different, rounder figure. The specific decimal has been lifted from an unrelated instrument and re-cited as the Treasury yield.

sentences.span: Less than 30% of S&P stocks are now above the 50-day moving average ... the index continues to prove resilient, even as the experience underneath it has become increasingly difficult
sentences.why: Source directly supports weak breadth beneath a resilient headline index — matches the sentence's characterization of damage spread across the average stock while a few names carry the index.

sentences.span: BoJ Policy Rate Sep 1.25% 1.00% ... The BoJ delivered a 25bp rate hike ... Sato and Asada dissented in favour of no policy change
sentences.why: The 1.25% new rate and the 2 named dissenters are supported (consistent with a 7-2 vote on a 9-member board). But no source states this is the 'highest since 1995', and no source connects dissenters Sato and Asada to appointments by Prime Minister Takaichi — that political attribution is fabricated.

sentences.span: The US August inflation reports came in above expectations, with core inflation accelerating by 0.3% month-on-month versus the 0.2% consensus forecast
sentences.why: Sources describe the August core print as coming in hot/above expectations (and 'uncomfortable' per 17189) — the opposite direction of the sentence's claim that the print (1.7%) came in below the 1.8% expected. The specific 1.7%/1.8% figures and the UBS/Goldman January 2027 next-move call do not appear in any source.
